name: Alavanca

contrastIssues: #587291 (accent) on #EFEFEF bg → 3.8:1 — fails WCAG AA for body text (needs 4.5:1), passes only for 18pt+ bold
#463939 warm gray conflicts tonally with #223855 cool navy — two dark neutrals fighting for the same role
colorAudit.harmonyType: fractured-cool — navy primary (#223855) with no true accent, supported by unrelated warm gray (#463939)
colorAudit.hierarchyStatus: weak — no single dominant brand color wins. Primary navy is used only for H1s, buttons default to generic dark gray, no true accent color exists to drive CTAs
colorAudit.saturationNotes: Entire palette is under-saturated and low-energy — wrong temperature for a combat-sports brand. No heat, no urgency, nothing that says 'fight gym.'
colorAudit.modeMismatch: Current site uses light gray (#EFEFEF) bg, but the positioning is combat sports / 'Decide to Rise' / champions forged — this calls for a dark, high-contrast treatment, not a corporate light gray. The current light mode is the primary visual problem.

correctionStrategy: Keep Alavanca's navy (#223855) as the foundation of identity — deepen it into the background system so the brand color carries through the whole site instead of just H1s. Flip from light to dark mode (Rule 4 exception: the current light palette is clearly broken for a combat-sports brand). Introduce an electric amber accent as the 'one electric accent' that performance-athletic-skill requires — amber sits near-complementary to cool navy on the color wheel, giving the sportswear-brand warm/cool split that reads as high-energy athletic.

contrastVerification.accent-on-bg: 9.2:1 — AAA pass (large text + UI), AA pass (body)
contrastVerification.bg-on-accent-button: 9.2:1 — button text (dark on amber) reads clean
contrastVerification.border-on-bg: 1.4:1 — decorative only (OK, borders are not text)

colorShifts: Flipped light → dark mode. Current #EFEFEF bg was fighting the combat-sports positioning; deep navy-tinted black (#0A1220) reads serious, athletic, and lets photography pop.
Preserved Alavanca's existing navy (#223855) as the card / elevated surface color — their brand color now carries through every section, not just H1s.

Introduced electric amber (#F59E0B) as the new accent. This IS a new color (the original palette had no true accent), but it's chosen as a near-complement to navy — a classic sportswear warm/cool pairing (think Under Armour, New Balance running). Signals energy, urgency, 'Decide to Rise.'
Dropped the warm gray (#463939) — it was tonally fighting the navy and added nothing. Cleaner to use navy as the only dark color family.
Kept the existing lighter navy (#587291) as --brand-navy-light for subtle hover tints and secondary accents so it still feels like Alavanca.

fontRecommendation.display: Bold compressed display — Anton, Archivo Black, or Bebas Neue — uppercase, tight tracking, for headlines like 'DECIDE TO RISE' and 'CHAMPIONS FORGED'
fontRecommendation.body: Inter 400–700 or Manrope — clean modern sans, 15–17px body size
fontRecommendation.numeric: Tabular numbers for class schedules / location cards
fontRecommendation.reasoning: Performance-athletic-skill mandates a bold sportswear-brand type system: display sans in compressed caps for kinetic marquees and hero, readable humanist sans for body. Keeps the 'athletic brand' feeling without leaning into fight-poster brutalism or heritage serif territory.

identityCheck: The brand still reads as Alavanca — their navy is everywhere (backgrounds, cards, elevated surfaces, hover states). What's new is the amber accent that pushes CTAs and kinetic moments, and the dark mode treatment that matches combat-sports positioning. If you put this next to their current site, a member would recognize it immediately as a deeper, more confident version of the same brand.
